framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations Reg 10 / Commissioner materials Accreditation and Certification Framework
clause_or_page: D p.5 'Why is the Framework necessary?'; p.4
requirement_paraphrase: Framework says the Regulations bar commercial use of Systems for High Risk Processing unless audit and certification requirements are met; applicant defined as 'Certification Applicant'.
what_is_tested: Compliance of High Risk Processing Systems with certification requirements

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Continuously assess the cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents throughout the development lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.
what_is_tested: Pre-market and periodic testing of AI-content marking and detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.
what_is_tested: Third-party post-market evaluation access and safe harbour

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
clause_or_page: Appendix A.1.5 Structured Public Feedback, p.49-51
requirement_paraphrase: Describes participatory engagement, field testing and AI red-teaming as structured feedback methods; red-team quality depends on team expertise; diverse, interdisciplinary red teams with domain expertise are suggested; types are general public, expert, combination, and human/AI.
who_tests: Red teams (public, expert, mixed, or AI-assisted)

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and testing data must be governed by documented practices including examination for biases and measures to detect and mitigate them; data sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative, as error-free and complete as possible, and reflect the geographic, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of intended use.
what_is_tested: Data quality, representativeness and bias of train/validation/test sets

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing requires a testing plan submitted to the market surveillance authority and approved (tacitly after 30 days unless national law requires authorisation), registration with a unique EU identification number, and a duration of at most six months extendable by six more.
what_is_tested: Authorisation and registration of real-world tests

framework: Abu Dhabi Law No. (3) of 2024 establishing the AI and Advanced Technology Council
requirement_paraphrase: The Council sets the conditions, controls, standards and systems that must be observed in AI investment and research, and follows the performance and feasibility of AI-related policies. The law gives no explicit power to test AI systems.
what_is_tested: None directly (policies and standards-setting; performance of policies)

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit self-assessment tool (Digital Dubai)
clause_or_page: Page sections 'What is the self-assessment tool for?' and 'What does it contain?'
requirement_paraphrase: Developer or operator organisations can self-assess an AI system's ethics level against Dubai's AI Ethics Guidelines across fairness, accountability, transparency and explainability, after classifying the system as non-significant, significant or critical; the tool reports gaps and suggests mitigations. Guidelines are recommended, not mandatory; the tool is in beta.
what_is_tested: AI system ethics level and gaps across four aspects

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Once released, keep ongoing performance monitoring with evidence that the system operates as expected; use managed release processes with the ability to withdraw and revert; monitor for model drift.

Technical report surveying how trust in AI can be built through transparency, explainability and controllability, engineering pitfalls and threats, and approaches to assessing and improving properties such as resilience, safety, security and privacy; does not define trustworthiness levels; published 28 May 2020, 43 pages.
